recap.workouts:
CrossFit, 06:40, 45:53, avg HR 112 / max 142, RPE 5, load 13 — the cheapest gym day of the week. Front squat went to 245 lb, which you call your current 1RM, well past the ~85% cap I asked for. You named it straight: test week, you wanted the number that sets the whole 8-week cycle, so you kept seven of the ten sets very light and took only three heavy singles, then kept the wall balls and the rope at an easy pace. The file agrees with the story — 46 minutes at an average of 112 bpm and a load of 13 is a barbell day, not a metcon day.

Hypertrophy, arms and delts (triceps 3/3), all four lifts at the prescribed 2 sets:
Barbell curl 40 × 12, 40 × 12 — top of the range on both, so 45 lb next arms day.
Triceps pushdown 80 × 15, 80 × 13 on the new handle. That is the baseline I refused to invent for you, now logged. 15 then 13 means the all-sets rule is not met, so 80 lb holds.
Lateral raise 20 × 20, 20 × 15. Across the week that is 20/18/18 on Wednesday plus 20/15 today — two of five sets at the top. 20 lb holds, exactly as the plan's note predicted it might.
Rear delt / face pull 85 × 15, 85 × 15 — bottom of the 15–20 range at the newly bumped load, so 85 holds. Your note that the shoulders were sore for no obvious reason is consistent with that; nothing to act on yet, just logged.

RCI8 — 70:02, 13.08 km, load 78, avg HR 149 / max 170, RPE 6, paired at 98.7% compliance. Analysed off the full per-second streams.

First, the structure. Your saved file had 5′ and 19′ of Zone 2 instead of 10′ and 14′. Total time unchanged, the 4 × 6′ core untouched — the reps are the session and they were fully intact. The one place it mattered is rep 1, which you started off a five-minute Zone 2 lead-in rather than ten.

The four reps, target band 4:22–4:42/km, first 60 s of each dropped:
rep 1 — 4:30/km · HR 153 → 154, max 158 · slope +1.3 bpm/min · decoupling 6.5%
rep 2 — 4:28/km · HR 154 → 163, max 164 · slope +2.0 · decoupling 6.6%
rep 3 — 4:23/km · HR 159 → 164, max 169 · slope +1.2 · decoupling 3.2%
rep 4 — 4:28/km · HR 159 → 165, max 170 · slope +0.9 · decoupling 4.4%

Seven seconds per kilometre of spread across four reps, every one inside the band, the fastest one third from the end. You wrote that you followed the pace target for every zone — you did, and it is the tightest set of reps in the file this block.

The heart-rate story. Plateau HR climbs 154 → 163 → 164 → 165 across the set. Read that carefully rather than as one number: rep 1 was run off a half-length warm-up and was still arriving, which is most of the 154 → 163 step. From rep 2 onward you gained two beats across eighteen minutes of work at the same pace. And the within-rep slope falls every single rep — 2.0, then 1.2, then 0.9 — which is HR settling into the effort, not running away from it. Against the run-measured LTHR of 167, you spent 2.3 minutes of the whole seventy at or above it, peaking at 170 in the last rep.

Recoveries, which you asked me to read with the terrain in mind: 6:50 · 7:11 · 7:24 · 7:29 per km, HR down to 129 · 133 · 136 · 141 by the end of each. The floor creeps up four to five beats a time, which is normal accumulation across four threshold reps, and you were still shedding roughly 25–30 beats inside every three-minute jog. 82 m of climbing over the run, nothing steep enough to explain any of it away.

The 19′ Zone 2 tail: 5:18/km, average HR 153, HR slope +0.39 bpm/min, decoupling 0.4%. After twenty-four minutes of threshold work that is essentially a flat line.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: this is the best-executed run of the block, and the anchors RT19 established on 30 July just passed their first real test. Four reps at 4:23–4:30 against a 4:22–4:42 band, HR sitting just under LTHR the whole way with only 2.3 minutes at or above 167, and within-rep drift shrinking rep on rep rather than growing. That is a threshold set run AT threshold, not above it — which is exactly what 167 being the right number looks like. Consequence: proceed, nothing to protect against. Confidence high; this is per-second stream data, not averages.

2) The tail is the quiet headline. The plan flagged the 14′ (yours ran 19′) Zone 2 tail as where the week's Zone X record usually dies. It came in at 5:18/km, mid-band, with a heart-rate slope of +0.39 bpm/min and 0.4% decoupling after 24 minutes of threshold work. Full disclosure on the number: per-second pace scatter puts 4.6 minutes in the Zone X band, and that is transition time entering and leaving eight zone changes plus rolling terrain — the rep means and the tail mean are all where they should be. This was not a medium session.

3) The front squat, honestly, both directions. You took 245 against my cap and the run came back clean, so today the evidence is yours. But be clear about what actually protected it: you bought the single by scaling everything around it — seven light sets, an easy Reeves, load 13, average HR 112. That is not ignoring the cap, that is paying for the number somewhere else, and it worked. The version that would have cost you is taking 245 AND racing the nine minutes. Keep doing it your way and I will stay out of it.

4) ADAPT: no-op. RCI8 EXECUTED at 98.7% compliance and full structure, CrossFit MODIFIED but cheap by load and HR, hypertrophy done at the prescribed set counts. Nothing in the weekend moves and nothing is owed. Five days into week 9, both hard sessions delivered.
recap.tomorrow:

The only way to get this wrong is speed. The day after four threshold reps your legs will happily settle into 4:50s and that is Zone X — full fatigue cost, no adaptation, and the exact leak that cost week 8 its 80/20. You already ran the answer today: the 19-minute tail came in at 5:18/km with a flat heart rate. Repeat that pace for eighty minutes and the week closes clean.

Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
